name: Sweet Spot Rate
summary: The share of batted balls with a launch angle between 8 and 32 degrees.
easy: When people say a ball came off the sweet spot of the bat, they mean it was hit square. Statcast defined it by launch angle instead of a spot on the bat: anything between 8 and 32 degrees, roughly line drives and low fly balls.
Balls in that range don't die in the infield like grounders or float up harmlessly like pop-ups. A higher rate means a hitter keeps sending the ball out at angles that tend to become hits.

scale.note: Distribution of the 135 qualified hitters in 2026.

deep: It only looks at the angle, not how hard the ball was hit. That's why the MLB glossary suggests pairing it with hard-hit rate (95 mph or more). Barrels are the category that combines speed and angle.

Two hitters can have the same average launch angle while one sends most balls between 8 and 32 degrees and the other alternates between grounders and pop-ups. Sweet spot rate shows that difference right away.
On Baseball Savant leaderboards it's labeled LA SwSp%.
